patches.summary: With a recording request and a recorded startup page, this reuses replay's sequence from browser.ts:153-160: probe the chrome:// pages on the startup page, close it, run the realpath/lstat checks on its video (no symlink, regular file, dirname equal to realpath(recording.dir)), delete it, require readdir(recording.dir) to be empty, open a fresh page that must be about:blank (otherwise TARGET_DRIFT), then video = newPage.video() and recording.ready(video !== null). `page` and `video` rebind to the new page, so the CDP session, crash, route, blank proof, handle.page and recordedVideo() all see it. Any check or delete failure throws inside the existing try, and the existing GuidedLaunchFailure cleanup ends the launch closed. When there is no recording, or the startup page has no video, the code calls recording?.ready(false) and probes the single page as it does today. No new mechanism, no deadline, and no contract, schema or wire change.

Docs only, as the ruling's change.files[1] requires. It restates readiness as 'after the startup probe recording is deleted and the fresh app page exists (replay semantics, AR-QA SEC-001)'. It is optional for the fix, but without it the Javadoc says the opposite of the code.

Oracle A: decode the uploaded objects/studio/fixture-csi/guided/{sessionId}.webm at full resolution with `ffmpeg -t a0/1000 -vsync 0 -pix_fmt rgb24 -f rawvideo` (no scale filter), where a0 = timings[0].startMs. Assert the output is not empty and every byte is >= 245. Oracle B: decode up to a0+1000 ms, map the first byte below 245 to its frame index and that frame's ffprobe best_effort_timestamp_time (t1), then assert -250 <= t1-a0 <= 500. A missing paint in that window fails. Oracle C, in the AC-1 parity case: handle.page.url() is 'about:blank' before the first navigation, and before close, recording dir holds exactly one file whose name is basename(recordedVideo()). Facts {a0, t1, t1-a0, prefix frame count, first non-white frame index, probed frames} are written to docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-013/r13/sec001-guided-video-oracle.json before the asserts, so a red run is also recorded. Paths are redacted. The decoding is the same ffmpeg/ffprobe execFileSync as observed-bootstrap-video.test.ts, with the same eslint-disable justification. No new dependency. A missing ffmpeg/ffprobe throws, so the test fails and never skips.

The other v1 failures under load 40+ were NO_FIRST_PAINT (navigate took 6-12 s, beyond a0+1 s) and one TARGET_CHANGED. That is an extreme-load environment and not this oracle. B would also fail there, by design (the seek budget).
oracleRevision.rootCause: Playwright 1.63 videoRecorder writes each screencast frame at frameSwapWallTime minus recorder creation, and ffmpeg starts the output at the first frame it receives. The webm therefore starts at the first composited frame, not at ready(). When about:blank composites no frame before navigation, the app's own first paint, or the initial solid surface, is frame 0 at pts 0, which is before a0. v1 oracle A ("every frame before a0 is white") assumed video zero equals the origin, so it contradicted B, which allows t1 down to a0-250.
oracleRevision.change: Oracle A, v2: decode [0, a0+1 s] at full resolution. Every frame must be either CONTENT-FREE (every row has at most 6 solid-colour runs at per-channel tolerance 12; white has 1 and the initial surface 2, while text rows have 55-437) or must show NO non-white pixel outside the APP REGION. The app region is the union of two boxes, padded by 8 px. The first is the login page's box, measured independently by a separate recorded guided launch of the same Chromium at the same size, navigated to /login (last decoded frame). The second is this run's own settled final frame (the home page, decoded with -sseof -1). B keeps -250 <= t1-a0 <= 500, with t1 = the pts of the first non-content-free frame. Facts are written before the asserts: per-frame ms, box, maxRowRuns, contentFree, outsideApp, the region, a0 and t1.
oracleRevision.whyNotVacuous: Startup-probe footage is text over most of the viewport. Red re-proof with only sec001-browser.patch reverted (3/3 RED): frames 2-4 at pts 80-160 ms have maxRowRuns 437, box [240,6,1039,719] and about 91k px outside the app region [0,0,408,~100]. Decoded, they are chrome://version (Chrome for Testing build, command line and profile path). Evidence: sec001-red2-oracle.json. The PNG stays in scratch only because it shows a local path. Frame 0 in red is the initial surface and is correctly content-free.
oracleRevision.proposedRulingText: AR-QA SEC-001 proofOracles.A_startupFramesAbsent (amended): decode the uploaded webm at full resolution over [0, a0+1000 ms]. Every frame is either content-free (no row with more than 6 solid-colour runs at per-channel tolerance 12) or has no non-white pixel (any channel < 245) outside the app region. The app region is the union of the login page's non-white box, measured by a separate recorded guided launch of the same Chromium, and the run's settled final frame's box, padded by 8 px. Reason: Playwright's webm starts at the first composited frame, not at ready(), so frames before a0 can legitimately show the app's first paint or Chromium's initial solid surface. B_trimBeforeOffsets is unchanged, with t1 = the first non-content-free frame.
